text.p: Transitional Hospitals Corp said Tuesday its board voted to postpone the "distribution date" under its stockholder rights plan until the earlier of either June 17 or the date an acquiring person acquires 15 percent of the company's outstanding common stock.
Without the board's action, the rights would have become exercisable Tuesday, June 10, Transitional's statement said without explanation.
Company officials were not available to elaborate.

On May 19, the company said it was trying to preserve the Select Medical deal to take the company private for $14.55 per share while exploring the possibility of accepting the $16 per share offered by Vencor Inc.
Pursuant to the rights plan, following the distribution date, stockholders have the right to purchase 1/100 of a share of Series B Junior Participating Preferred Stock for $45.00.

Transitional's statement said the plan further provides that if Vencor were to acquire 15 percent of the outstanding common stock, stockholders, other than Vencor, would have the right to purchase common stock having a value of $90.00 for $45.00. The board has previously amended the distribution date on two other occasions, the statement pointed out.
